english.title: Contravene direction re disclosure - terrorism
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that a direction under section 18 of the Anti-terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001 had been issued by the Secretary of State prohibiting the disclosure of any information in relation to

(A)_[proceedings overseas,]_
(B)_[any description of overseas proceedings,]_

disclosed information in contravention of that direction
english.legislation: Contrary to section 18(6) of the Anti-Terrorism, Crime and Security Act 2001.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: A direction under this section -(a) may prohibit the making of disclosures absolutely or in such cases, or subject to such conditions as to consent or otherwise, as may be specified in it; and (b) must be published or otherwise issued by the Secretary of State in such manner as he considers appropriate for bringing it to the attention of persons likely to be affected by it. (Section 18(5))

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
